title: Entropy and Nondiagonal Asymptotic Pairs
answer: No: a previously published expansive algebraic counterexample has positive entropy and only diagonal asymptotic pairs.

attribution.author: Tom Meyerovitch
attribution.reference: Theorem 1.2 and Section 4, Pseudo-orbit tracing and algebraic actions of countable amenable groups

exact_scope: Every countably infinite amenable discrete group acting expansively by continuous automorphisms on a compact metrizable abelian group; asymptotic means convergence outside finite subsets of the whole group.
witness_group: G = direct sum for n>=1 of (F_2)^(n+1)
witness_space: Closed subgroup of F_2^G satisfying zero sum on every translate of each coordinate factor H_n.
asymptotic_pairs: All diagonal; the only finitely supported element of X is zero.
